Campaign Landing Page Brief for Varanasi Businesses: Before You Pay for Traffic

Turn a campaign idea into an accountable landing-page brief that separates ad clicks, page activity, received enquiries and qualified conversations.

By SiteSutra · 29 October 2026

← All articlesYour next step ↓

Paying for traffic cannot repair an unclear offer, a broken enquiry route or a page that does not match the campaign promise. Before a Varanasi business starts a paid campaign, its landing page needs one audience, one useful next action and a tested way to receive the response.

A campaign brief makes those decisions reviewable before media spend begins. It also separates the landing-page build, campaign management and advertising budget so the business knows who owns each part.

Define the business outcome before the channel

Start with the service or action the campaign should support. “Get more leads” is too broad to design or measure. A useful outcome names the intended visitor, the offer, the next action and what makes an enquiry qualified.

  • Audience: who should reach the page and which location or service need applies.
  • Offer: what the business can genuinely provide, including important limits.
  • Next action: call, WhatsApp, form submission or booking.
  • Qualification: the information needed to decide whether the request fits.
  • Owner: the person who receives, checks and follows up on the enquiry.

Keep the page focused on the campaign decision. The main website can explain the wider business; the landing page should help this audience understand the offer, verify the relevant facts and take the agreed next step.

Match the campaign promise to the destination

The campaign wording, destination URL and page content should describe the same offer. Google Ads requires destinations to be functional, useful, easy to navigate and accessible to its crawler, and it restricts destination mismatches and pages that do not work in common browsers or devices. These are platform requirements, not evidence that a campaign will perform.

Check the promise before launch
Campaign promiseLanding-page evidenceAcceptance check
A defined serviceScope, location, exclusions and next step.The visitor can confirm whether the service fits without guessing.
A consultation or bookingDuration, availability, timezone and working booking destination.A test booking reaches the correct calendar and confirmation path.
A call or messageVisible business identity, contact details and response expectation.The link opens the correct number or channel on a phone.
A form enquiryOnly the fields needed to respond and qualify.A real test submission reaches the named recipient.

Hypothetical example: a Varanasi home-service campaign

Imagine a fictional Varanasi air-conditioner servicing business planning a campaign for scheduled maintenance. This is an original planning example, not a SiteSutra client project or a performance claim.

The first brief targets residents within the business's verified service area who want to request a maintenance slot. The page explains the included inspection, the types of units accepted, the coverage area and the information required before confirming a visit. Its main action is a short enquiry form; a phone link remains available for urgent questions.

The form asks for name, contact number, locality, unit type and preferred day. The business owner receives a test submission before launch and records whether the request can be served. The page reports the campaign click, landing-page visit, form submission, received enquiry and qualified enquiry as different events. No booking or sale is assumed from a button click.

Test the entire enquiry route

  1. Open the campaign destination on a phone and desktop browser.
  2. Check that the heading and offer match the campaign wording.
  3. Use every call, message, booking and form action.
  4. Confirm the receiving person gets the test enquiry with the expected details.
  5. Check the confirmation or error state and the visitor's next step.
  6. Record who follows up, when and how qualification is decided.

A visual success message is not delivery evidence. If a form provider, calendar or notification service is not configured, keep that dependency visible and do not launch the campaign as if it were working.

Make the response path understandable and accessible

Use persistent labels, identify required fields and explain expected formats before a visitor submits. W3C advises that labels and instructions help people understand form controls, while placeholder text should not replace a label. Error messages should identify the affected field and explain how to correct it.

Test the page with a keyboard, visible focus, zoom and a narrow viewport. Important information and the enquiry action should remain available without animation. Obtain permission for customer photographs, reviews or logos; do not use invented proof to fill a campaign page.

Name each measure and its source

Campaign tags can identify a referring campaign in analytics. Google's URL builder guidance describes parameters such as source, medium and campaign, and recommends consistent values. Agree a naming pattern before links are distributed, then document the actual analytics property and event configuration.

Keep activity and business outcomes separate
StagePossible sourceWhat it does not prove
Ad clickAdvertising platformThat the page loaded or the visitor understood the offer.
Landing-page sessionConfigured website analyticsThat an enquiry was sent or received.
Form or booking actionWebsite or booking eventThat the notification arrived or the request was suitable.
Received enquiryInbox, phone, calendar or customer systemThat the enquiry was qualified or became a customer.
Qualified enquiryBusiness review against agreed criteriaA guaranteed sale or campaign result.

Search visibility, AI citation checks and paid-campaign activity are separate evidence sets. Do not combine them into one success number.

Separate the commercial responsibilities

A proposal should state whether it covers strategy, copy, design, development, form or booking integration, analytics configuration, advertising-platform setup, creative production, campaign management and ongoing optimisation. Advertising media spend should be shown separately from service fees. Platform accounts and payment methods should remain with the business owner unless another arrangement is explicitly agreed.

Record the review rounds, launch authority, campaign end date and maintenance owner. A landing page can be built and tested without promising traffic, rankings, clicks or qualified enquiries.

Download the campaign landing-page brief

Download the campaign landing-page brief (CSV). It includes blank decision fields and a clearly labelled hypothetical example covering audience, offer, destination, enquiry delivery, campaign tags and acceptance evidence.

Replace the example with verified business information. Keep passwords, customer data and payment details in the relevant provider's access controls rather than the worksheet.

Make the landing page ready before paying for traffic

Approve the audience, offer, destination, receiving owner and measurement stages. Then test one complete enquiry from campaign link to business response before the campaign begins.
